candidate_sentences.text: AS LHV Pank posted a consolidated net profit of EUR 24.3 million in Q2 2026, benefiting from loan growth and cloud-infrastructure migration, although earnings were impacted by higher impairment charges.
Overall, the period was characterized by steady core revenue growth and strategic business advancements, balanced against higher provisioning costs and shifting deposit volumes.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital adequacy ratio of 20.8% (vs 22.4% at end-2025) and liquidity coverage ratio of 171.5% (vs 185.0% at end-2025), with core Tier 1 ratio at 15.81% and Tier 1 ratio at 17.49%.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: The Group's Liquidity, Capitalisation and Asset Quality section and Note 16.

candidate_sentences.text: Capital adequacy stood at 20.8% at the end of Q2 2026, remaining well above internal and regulatory requirements.
Return on equity attributable to shareholders was 10.7% for the quarter, recovering from Q1 2026 levels but remaining below the 17.4% reported in Q2 2025.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating environment impacted by Middle East conflict de-escalation and energy price volatility, with OECD forecasting 2.8% global growth for 2026 contingent on Strait of Hormuz stability.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Operating Environment section: geopolitical tensions, energy prices, and OECD economic outlook.

verified_key_information_units.information: First half 2026 consolidated results: net profit EUR 44.4 million (-26% YoY), net income EUR 152.7 million (approximately flat YoY), and loan impairment charges EUR 7.1 million (vs EUR 1.5 million in H1 2025).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary tables for 6M 2026: net profit, net income, and impairment charges compared to 6M 2025.

candidate_sentences.text: For the first six months of 2026, the Group's net profit reached EUR 44.4 million, compared with EUR 59.3 million for the same period in 2025.

verified_key_information_units.information: Loan and bond portfolio impairment charges increased to EUR 5.8 million in Q2 2026 (from EUR 1.3 million in Q1 2026 and EUR -4.2 million in Q2 2025), driven by model-based forward-looking provisions.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary and Note 20: impairment charges for Q2 2026 and comparisons with prior periods.

candidate_sentences.text: The Group recorded higher loan and bond provisions of EUR 5.8 million in Q2 2026, up from EUR 1.3 million in the previous quarter, driven by model-based, forward-looking impairment charges.

verified_key_information_units.information: Managed funds increased to EUR 1,790 million (+4% QoQ, +15% YoY) with LHV Varahaldus reporting strong Q2 performance in index funds, while actively managed pension funds showed mixed results.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Overview of AS LHV Varahaldus section: fund volumes, active clients, and performance of pension funds.

candidate_sentences.text: AS LHV Varahaldus contributed a net profit of EUR 0.4 million, supported by growth in assets under management to nearly EUR 1.8 billion, despite a slight decrease in active second-pillar clients.

verified_key_information_units.information: Performance against financial plan: Q2 net income slightly below plan due to higher expenses, loan portfolio growth according to plan, but deposits remained below plan.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary section: Management Board commentary on plan variances.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers most HIGH importance criteria: Q2 2026 headline financial performance (K1), loan portfolio and deposit changes (K2), subsidiary profits (K3), strategic developments (K4), capital adequacy ratios (K5), first half results (K7), loan/bond provisions (K8), and managed funds performance (K9). However, it lacks explicit mention of the operating environment impacts from the Middle East conflict and energy prices (K6), and does not address performance against the financial plan regarding net income, loan growth, and deposits (K10). These omissions affect the completeness assessment, but the majority of core material information is present, justifying a 'Generally yes' rating.

coherence_issues.description: S1 and S4 report different figures for consolidated net profit/income in Q2 2026 (EUR 24.7 million vs EUR 79.0 million) without explanation. This creates an unresolved logical gap as the summary does not clarify the relationship or reconcile these divergent figures.

candidate_sentences.text: AS LHV Group reported a consolidated net profit of EUR 24.7 million for the second quarter of 2026, representing an increase of EUR 5 million compared with the first quarter of 2026, but a decrease of EUR 6.1 million compared with the second quarter of 2025.
The Group's consolidated net income for Q2 2026 amounted to EUR 79.0 million, reflecting a 7.3% increase over Q1 2026 and a slight increase compared with EUR 73.9 million in Q2 2025.

details.coherence_justification: The summary is generally coherent with consistent structure and logical flow across most statements. However, S1 reports consolidated net profit of EUR 24.7 million for Q2 2026 while S4 reports consolidated net income of EUR 79.0 million for the same period, creating an unexplained discrepancy. No clarification is provided about whether these represent different measures (e.g., before/after tax, different accounting treatments) or if one is a typo. This represents a material logical gap. Other elements show appropriate comparisons, clear organization, and no self-contradictions or significant repetition.
